svg.title: Where kakapo live
svg.desc: A simplified map of New Zealand. Kakapo survive on small islands where introduced cats, rats and stoats have been removed, including Whenua Hou or Codfish Island near Stewart Island and Anchor Island in Dusky Sound in Fiordland. Three males also live behind a predator fence at Sanctuary Mountain Maungatautari in the North Island. The population has risen from 51 birds in 1995 to more than 236.

text.font-family: Georgia, serif
-apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: New Zealand only, and almost all of it on islands cleared of cats, rats and stoats.

svg.text: A simplified diagram, not to scale. Ten males moved to the mainland fence in 2023 and three still live there, the first kakapo on the mainland in almost forty years.
